title: The Ministry of Reconciliation
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Need for Reconciliation
subpoints: Humanity is separated from God due to the sin of Adam and personal transgressions.
Sinners are described as enemies of God, lacking the initiative to seek Him.
God takes the initiative to reconcile, meeting humanity in their state of enmity.

outline.title: The Source of Reconciliation
subpoints: All things pertaining to salvation proceed from God.
God reconciled believers to Himself through Jesus Christ.
The transformation of Paul from persecutor to apostle exemplifies this divine initiative.

outline.title: The Message of Reconciliation
subpoints: God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself, not imputing their trespasses.
The term 'world' refers to all kinds of people, not necessarily every individual.
Christ is the sole mediator between God and man, offering a ransom for all.

outline.title: The Ministry of Reconciliation
subpoints: Believers are appointed as ambassadors for Christ.
The church is called to plead on Christ's behalf for sinners to be reconciled to God.
The work of reconciliation was accomplished completely at the cross ('It is finished').

summary:
This sermon explores the profound doctrine of reconciliation as presented in 2 Corinthians 5:18-21. The message begins by establishing the necessity of reconciliation, highlighting that humanity is separated from God due to the inherited sin of Adam and personal transgressions. Unlike human conflicts where both parties may seek peace, the biblical narrative emphasizes that God takes the sole initiative to bridge the divide, reaching out to sinners who are described as enemies of God.

The sermon identifies God as the source of this reconciliation, noting that all aspects of salvation proceed from Him. This is illustrated through the life of the Apostle Paul, who was transformed from a persecutor of the church into a devoted ambassador for Christ. This transformation underscores the power of God's grace to reconcile even the most hostile hearts to Himself.

The core message of reconciliation is that God, in Christ, has reconciled the world to Himself, not imputing their trespasses. The text clarifies that this refers to the availability of reconciliation for all kinds of people, with Jesus Christ serving as the sole mediator. Finally, the sermon outlines the ministry of reconciliation, calling believers to act as ambassadors who implore others to be reconciled to God, recognizing that the work of atonement was fully accomplished at the cross.
